answer.label: Attributed to — shortened wording
answer.sourceLine: The unofficial Munger Archive calls this short version an attribution rather than a verbatim recording. Stripe Press’s book contains a fuller two-part rule: “Take a simple, basic idea” and “take it very seriously.” The short display is also used by the publisher, but its original occasion remains unconfirmed.

author.heading: About Charlie Munger
author.bio: Charlie Munger trained as a lawyer and became Warren Buffett’s long-term investing partner at Berkshire Hathaway. He also chaired Wesco Financial and the Daily Journal Corporation. His public talks combine business examples with psychology, mathematics and lessons about practical judgment.

lead: The fuller rule occurs in an argument about taking elementary ideas seriously across disciplines. Munger calls it an old two-part rule rather than claiming exclusive invention. The familiar short form preserves the gist while reducing his wording. Publisher’s full book text ↗
